concept.name: Moving average convergence divergence
concept.definition: Gerald Appel's Moving Average Convergence/Divergence oscillator (late 1970s): a momentum indicator built from the difference between a fast and a slow EMA (default 12 and 26) with a 9-period EMA signal line, combining trend-following and momentum information in one unbounded oscillator.
concept.intuition: When the fast average pulls away from the slow one, momentum is accelerating; when they converge, the move is running out of steam.
concept.mechanics: MACD line = EMA(12) - EMA(26) of closes; signal line = 9-period EMA of the MACD line; histogram = line minus signal. Signals include signal-line crossovers, zero-line (centerline) crossovers — equivalent to the underlying EMA crossover — and divergences with price.
concept.formula: MACD = EMA_12(Close) - EMA_26(Close); Signal = EMA_9(MACD); Histogram = MACD - Signal.
concept.failure_modes: Signal-line crossovers whipsaw in flat or volatile markets, and crossovers at extremes often mark momentum exhaustion rather than reversal; being unbounded, MACD cannot flag overbought or oversold conditions.
concept.misconceptions: MACD is not a bounded oscillator, so high readings are not inherently overbought; nor does a signal-line cross guarantee a trend change.
concept.example: If the 12-day EMA is 102 and the 26-day EMA is 100, MACD = +2; with a 9-day signal line at 1.5, the histogram reads +0.5.
